name: Festus
summary: The governor who took Felix's place and found Paul still a prisoner. When Paul appealed to Caesar, Festus agreed to send him, and he laid Paul's case before King Agrippa.

key_moments.title: Takes Over from Felix
key_moments.description: After two years Festus took the place of Felix, and the chief priests asked him to bring Paul to Jerusalem, planning to kill him on the way. Festus said Paul would be kept at Caesarea, and his accusers could come there.

key_moments.title: Grants Paul's Appeal to Caesar
key_moments.description: Festus heard the case at Caesarea and, wanting to please the Jews, asked Paul if he would be judged in Jerusalem. Paul appealed to Caesar, and after speaking with his council, Festus said that to Caesar he would go.

key_moments.title: Telling King Agrippa
key_moments.description: When King Agrippa and Bernice visited, Festus told him about Paul, a prisoner left behind by Felix, whose case was about a man named Jesus who had died but whom Paul said was alive. Agrippa wished to hear Paul himself.

key_moments.title: Festus Calls Paul Mad
key_moments.description: As Paul spoke of Christ rising from the dead, Festus shouted that his great learning had made him mad. Paul answered that he was not mad but was speaking true and sober words.
